_comment: Progressive retirement of pre-reel ThemedShort videos. Two defect classes are tracked separately because they are not equally bad. CLASS A videos were published before commit 0971952 (2026-08-11 18:58 +0100, 'Stop the daily generator inventing statistics') and contain the removed stat beat: a number drawn at random from a per-niche pool, rendered at 300px under a caption like 'Mind the number.' The 11 Aug Nintendo video showed '5', which meant nothing. Those videos assert a false figure with the full visual authority of a statistic, which is the real credibility and policy exposure. CLASS B videos were published after the fix and invent nothing, but shipped in the rejected pastel ThemedShort format with an unsourced claim. Class A is retired first. Videos are UNLISTED, never deleted: the URL keeps working, so every action here is reversible, and unlisting is enough to remove them from the grid, from search and from recommendations. Batches are ~10 a week rather than one bulk pass so each one stays auditable.
policyBasis: YouTube inauthentic-content policy is assessed at CHANNEL level, so unsourced invented figures sitting on the grid are a risk to the whole account and not only to those videos.
method: Composio YOUTUBE_UPDATE_VIDEO (privacy_status=unlisted). NOTE: that tool also resets embeddable and publicStatsViewable to false; acceptable for videos being retired, but it is lossy — see scripts/youtube-cleanup.mjs, which preserves the full status object but needs a broader OAuth scope than the repo's current youtube.upload-only refresh tokens.

classB.note: Pastel format, no invented figure. Queued behind Class A.

classC.note: Duplicate re-uploads of the same fact (a distinct mass-production axis from A/B: the same claim posted 2-5 times). 53 duplicate extra copies detected across yt-bbmw0; the oldest instance of each fact is kept, newer copies retired. Includes the 'Flexbox replaced 90% of CSS layout hacks' group, which is ALSO an invented figure (the 90% is fabricated) and would qualify as Class A on the false-statistic test — retired first within this class for that reason.

_runCaveat: Batch 2 (2026-08-18T17:10Z) was a SAME-DAY SECOND director pass — cleanup-log.json is OneDrive cloud-only and was invisible to the Linux sandbox at the start of this run, so the earlier 16:45Z pass was not seen until git HEAD was read on the Windows side. Batch 2's 10 unlist calls were already issued (all reversible) before that reconciliation; they targeted the duplicate/fabricated-% class C, not the enumerated Class A set, so no A/B counts are affected. One video (rqyKMfB2BBM) overlapped batch 1 and was already unlisted — a harmless no-op, not re-listed here. Next scheduled pass should resume Class A (17 remaining) at the ~10/week cadence and NOT run a second batch the same day.

batches.note: Channel videoCount statistic lagged (72->71, 15->14) at read time; YouTube caches that counter. Per-video status is authoritative and was confirmed for all ten.

Same-day second pass (see _runCaveat). Targeted duplicate re-uploads keeping the oldest canonical copy of each fact, plus all 4 copies of the fabricated 'Flexbox 90%' claim. 10 calls issued; rqyKMfB2BBM was already unlisted in batch 1 (no-op), so 9 videos newly retired.
